problem.title: Find the target in a sorted array
problem.learningObjective: Binary search halves the search space on every comparison: compute mid, compare, discard one half, repeat.
problem.canonicalAlgorithm: Set lo=0, hi=n-1. While lo<=hi compute mid=(lo+hi)/2. If a[mid]==target stop. If a[mid]<target set lo=mid+1 else set hi=mid-1. If lo>hi the target is absent.

answerFormat.label: Enter the zero-based target index or the target value.

spec.objective: In the sunken vault corridor, binary search halves the search space on every comparison: compute mid, compare, discard one half, repeat.

theme.title: The obsidian vault of the sunken vault corridor — Sealed
theme.story: A band of lanterns has been laid out along the sunken vault corridor, and only one of them opens the obsidian vault. The trap resets itself the moment you touch it in the wrong order, so work strictly in order and never guess. This is Binary Search, and it has to be done by the book.

narration.intro: A band of lanterns has been laid out along the sunken vault corridor, and only one of them opens the obsidian vault. The trap resets itself the moment you touch it in the wrong order, so work strictly in order and never guess. This is Binary Search, and it has to be done by the book. Right now the sunken vault corridor holds 8 lanterns. The obsidian vault reads 50, and it is in there somewhere. Work one at a time; the hints spell out the plan if you want them.
hintPool: Everything in the sunken vault corridor is in order, so order is the tool here. You never need to look at every value to make progress.
A comparison here does not just answer yes or no — it produces a direction, and the direction is what decides everything after it.
Whatever is left is still in order, so a whole side of it can be ruled out at once. Being able to do that is the only reason this is quick.
Finishing is a result, not a guess. The program stops when the rule allows it to stop, and reports what it found.
Do not begin at either end. Begin at the value in the middle of what is left, because that is the one that rules out the most.
Hold your lantern next to the obsidian vault and ask which is bigger. Whichever side is bigger, the other side is finished.
narration.win: The obsidian vault gives. Every lantern in the sunken vault corridor was handled in the order the plan demanded — O(log n) in the worst case, O(1) of extra space, and not one step spent that the algorithm did not require.
narration.lose: The obsidian vault stays shut. The sunken vault corridor resets, but the lanterns are exactly where you left them, and so is the plan. Same rules, different order.
correctFlavour: One down in the sunken vault corridor.

debrief.summary: You worked the sunken vault corridor one lantern at a time until the obsidian vault resolved. What this problem is built to teach: Binary search halves the search space on every comparison: compute mid, compare, discard one half, repeat. The run is bounded by O(log n) time and O(1) extra space, and that bound comes from the algorithm rather than from how carefully you played.

actionMeaning.comparePair: inspect two lanterns against each other — the compare operation. Mechanically: Select two objects and declare lt / eq / gt between their values.
actionMeaning.choosePath: decide which side of the sunken vault corridor stays open — the choose-path operation. Mechanically: Pick one branch (e.g. left / right) to narrow the remaining search space.
actionMeaning.submitAnswer: commit the obsidian vault — the terminate operation. Mechanically: Commit the final answer: declare the result index, value, or outcome.
